question: Should OpenClaw sponsor `appGuidedAuth` as a public provider-plugin contract for native and remote onboarding once the two review defects and real-behavior proof gap are resolved?
rationale: The PR introduces a durable plugin API and multi-client provider-auth product surface; code review can validate its implementation but cannot decide whether maintainers want to support that contract long term.

options.title: Sponsor and finish the contract
options.body: Accept the manifest-driven direction, require the lease fix, public documentation, compatibility coverage, and current-head real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the new plugin surface
options.body: Keep existing CLI and key-based provider setup while maintainers reconsider whether native app-guided auth should become a supported plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and finish the contract
recommendation.body: Accept the manifest-driven direction, require the lease fix, public documentation, compatibility coverage, and current-head real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and most heavily maintained the current onboarding behavior and is the strongest history-backed owner for the product/API choice.
